### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **24** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx`  _(via defaultHeaders (literal, a string literal in CONNECTOR_CREDENTIAL_MAP_PATHS), providerConfig (literal, a string literal in CONNECTOR_CREDENTIAL_MAP_PATHS), /api/v1/automation/connectors (route, a path literal in acceptanceCriteria), /meta/connector/:name (route, a path literal in surface))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/external-datasources.mdx`  _(via providerConfig (literal, a string literal in CONNECTOR_CREDENTIAL_MAP_PATHS))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/odata-datasources.mdx`  _(via providerConfig (literal, a string literal in CONNECTOR_CREDENTIAL_MAP_PATHS))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/automation/connectors (route, a path literal in acceptanceCriteria), /meta/connector/:name (route, a path literal in surface))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via providerConfig (literal, a string literal in CONNECTOR_CREDENTIAL_MAP_PATHS), /api/v1/automation/connectors (route, a path literal in acceptanceCriteria))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via /meta/connector/:name (route, a path literal in surface))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **213** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **153** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **153**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **98** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cd065d3698db13969a28f46bf26f3e47e9ecc09c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8a12c36d9c75026b9b6c57f765ed033556ecbc9c` — the merge of head `41256e95b9caece74a323a166252f4ce52975732` into base `cd065d3698db13969a28f46bf26f3e47e9ecc09c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8a12c36d9c75026b9b6c57f765ed033556ecbc9c && git checkout 8a12c36d9c75026b9b6c57f765ed033556ecbc9c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin cd065d3698db13969a28f46bf26f3e47e9ecc09c 41256e95b9caece74a323a166252f4ce52975732 && git checkout -B drift-repro cd065d3698db13969a28f46bf26f3e47e9ecc09c && git merge --no-ff 41256e95b9caece74a323a166252f4ce52975732

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cd065d3698db13969a28f46bf26f3e47e9ecc09c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs cd065d3698db13969a28f46bf26f3e47e9ecc09c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `41256e95b9caece74a323a166252f4ce52975732`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/integration/connector-credential-redaction.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-type-redaction.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.connector-instance-auth-inline-secret-refused.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/connector-auth.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/integration/connector-auth-static-kinds.test.ts, packages/spec/src/integration/connector-credential-redaction.test.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-type-redaction.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/connector-meta-door-credential-hardening.dogfood.test.ts + packages/spec/src/integration/connector.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/strict-object.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-credential-fields.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-type-schemas.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/system/environment-artifact.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/17.connector-inline-authentication-publish-refused.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/metadata-redaction.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-credential-carry-forward.ts, packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts, packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/compile.ts, docs/adr/0143-outbound-connector-auth-is-open-tier.md, docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs

Face: a published schema (`packages/spec/src/**`) plus a declared narrowing, so the floor is every path of the diff outside the changeset; the net diff against `main` (merge-base `617dcf432`) is the nine files the API lists, 914 insertions, 10 deletions. Reviewed from the tree, not the PR body. Per the disclosure ruling this record names positions and refusals only.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The widened refusal set — right.** The four static kinds (`none`, `bearer`, `api-key`, `basic`) move from `z.object` to `strictObject`, which is `closedObject(z.object(shape, { error }).strict())`: the unknown-key refusal is terminal on every zod line, so a body carrying an undeclared key raises exactly one `unrecognized_keys` issue at `auth` and no second complaint from the entry's `superRefine`. The refused set is every key the kind's shape does not declare, not a denylist: an inline secret in any listed spelling, a non-secret key borrowed from another kind (`headerName` on `bearer`), and `credentialRef` on `none`. That is what ADR-0143 D3 ("publish keeps refusing an inline secret") and its Acceptance ("an inline secret on any variant is refused at publish with a located error") ask for, and what the changeset declares. The `guidance` keys on each shape are keys the shape rejects, so the alias-integrity audit holds; the message names the key and never the value.
2. **The doors — right, with one door the changeset does not name.** `DeclarativeConnectorEntrySchema` is reached by: `defineStack` (`stack.zod.ts`, `connectors: z.array(DeclarativeConnectorEntrySchema)`); `os validate`, `os compile`, `os lint score`, `scaffold-validate`, `author-time-rules` and `os migrate meta` (each a `safeParse` of `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema`); `PUT /api/v1/meta/connector/:name` (`metadata-type-schemas.ts` registers `connector` to this schema; the save door's gate `safeParse`s the author's body and mints `422 INVALID_METADATA` with structured `issues`; the dogfood pins the issue located at `auth` on all four kinds and that nothing is stored); Studio's client validation (`clientValidation.ts` resolves the same schema). A fourth door answers identically and is not named: the metadata plugin's artifact load at boot and on reload (`_parseAndRegisterArtifact`: `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema.parse` for a bare definition, and `EnvironmentArtifactSchema` whose `metadata` is `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema`). No artifact `os build` emitted carries an undeclared key, because `compile.ts` serializes `result.data`, the parsed stack, which the old `z.object` already stripped; only a hand-assembled artifact JSON would now refuse at boot where it stripped before. Not a defect; see ③ for the prose note.
3. **Previously stored rows keep loading and materializing — right.** No boot or reload path parses a `sys_metadata` row through the type schema: the protocol's overlay hydration registers the raw row, the one schema use on reads is `_diagnostics`, and nothing in runtime, rest, metadata-protocol or service-automation gates on `_diagnostics.valid`. The automation plugin reads `registry.listItems('connector')` and `getMetaItemsForExecution` (audience `execution`, no decoration), so a row holding an undeclared `auth` key still reaches the provider with `credentialRef` resolved as before; its served `_diagnostics` now reads `valid: false` naming `auth`, the inventory the changeset describes.
4. **Carry-forward on a save of the served form — right.** In `saveMetaItem` the schema gate judges the author's body first and `carryForwardRedactedCredentials` runs after every gate, immediately before the put; it re-grafts each withheld path only where the incoming body is indistinguishable from the served form, then runs the type's redactor over the grafted body and keeps a value only where the redactor still withholds it. So a label edit of a legacy row re-saves and keeps its inline value at rest, a body that writes `token` itself is refused on its own merits, and an explicit `defaultHeaders: {}` is the author's word (a cleared form is served as written, so it differs from the stored map and wins). The dogfood CONTROL pins the `defaultHeaders` round trip and the dispatch after it.
5. **The redactor reaches every read exit — right.** `connector` is a built-in beside `datasource`; precedence is explicit registration, then built-in, then the schema derivation, and the connector schema carries no `.meta({ credential })` marker, so no derived coverage is bypassed. Every consumer resolves through `getMetadataTypeRedactor`: the protocol's `decorateMetadataItems` (behind `getMetaItems`, `getMetaItem`, and `getMetaItemsPerPackage`, which `GET /packages/:id/export` reads), the `/layers` read (code, overlay and effective bodies), the diff views, `redactStoredMetadataBody` / `redactStoredMetadataRow(s)` (the generic data door on `sys_metadata` and `sys_metadata_history`, the runtime reader seam, the MCP stdio bridge, the audit writers, the flow CRUD nodes) and `MetadataManager.getPublished`. The dogfood pins by name, `/layers`, both list spellings and the protocol's reads, for a member and an administrator.
6. **Fail-closed behaviour — right, one gap.** A `type` naming no kind, or no `type`, leaves `type` alone declared; an unknown `grant` or `scheme` keeps the keys its kind's siblings declare, none of which is a secret (the census pins the sixteen declared keys); a non-map value at a map position is withheld; a connector row whose body column will not parse as JSON now has its body withheld at the stored-row seam, where it was served as stored before (the type had no redactor). The gap: a non-object `auth` or `authentication` value (a string) is served as stored. No authoring door stores that shape (every door refuses it as `invalid_type`, before and after this change); only a system-context write reaches it. Should-fix, follow-up, in ④.
7. **Public surface unchanged — right.** `connector-credential-redaction.ts` is re-exported by no `index.ts`, and the package `exports` map has no wildcard subpath, so `redactConnectorItem`, `declaredConnectorAuthKeys` and `CONNECTOR_CREDENTIAL_MAP_PATHS` are shipped bytes, not published surface; `metadata-type-redaction.ts` exports the same names as before. The api-surface, declaration-map and export-origins baselines are untouched in the diff and `check:api-surface` is in the green Lint jobs.
8. **Generated artifacts consistent — right.** The strictness ledger shard counts object sites per directory from the AST (`shared/` = 26) and a `z.object` to `strictObject` swap at the same sites moves no count; the authorable-surface baseline records keys, the json-schema manifest records schema names, neither records posture. `check:generated` and `check:strictness-ledger` sit in the green Lint jobs on this head.
9. **Metadata-protocol narrowed on the read half too — right.** `/meta/connector` and the protocol's reads now serve a body without positions they served before (undeclared `auth` keys, `authentication` keys but `type`, the four maps whole). That is a served-shape narrowing and the `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` line covers it.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec: minor` with a BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, a FROM → TO block, and `adr-0087: registered connector-instance-auth-inline-secret-refused`. The level axis of `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` asks a `narrowed` declaration to grade at least one package whose published source moves `minor` or above and to sit beside the `(narrowing)` arm: both hold. The `registered` id resolves to `entries/semantic/18.connector-instance-auth-inline-secret-refused.ts`, whose four fields mirror the sibling `17.connector-inline-authentication-publish-refused.ts`; `check-adr-0087-registration` is in the green Lint jobs. Precedent: #28496 (`044d2016a`) declared a `@objectstack/spec` accept-set narrowing the same way (`minor`, `(narrowing)`, `registered`). The door-only narrowings in other packages that took `patch` are not this case: here a published schema's accept set moves and a semantic migration entry is owed. Declaration correct.

### ③ Boundary flags

The PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no author note is owed.

- **(1) Credential-looking values in `headers` / `defaultHeaders` at write, no refusal.** Accept as out of scope. A header value is a string the provider sends; refusing by shape would be a heuristic, and `lint-flow-credential-literals` is the precedent for an advisory rule. The read now withholds the maps, so such a value is at least no longer served. Follow-up card: an advisory `os lint` rule, not a door refusal.
- **(2) Read gating of `/api/v1/meta/connector` for members unchanged.** Escalate as a posture question, not blocking. The dogfood pins a member reads a connector `200` with every credential position withheld; the served body still carries `credentialRef` names, `baseUrl` and `transport.url`. Nothing here widens that read.
- **(3) Undeclared top-level connector keys stored and served.** Accept as out of scope. `ConnectorBaseSchema` is deliberately non-strict (its retirements are `retiredKey()` tombstones under ADR-0104), and a top-level key is not a credential position ADR-0097 §3 or ADR-0143 D3 names. If the shape is to close, that is the #4001 campaign's own ledger row, not this change.
- **(4) Maps withheld whole, non-credential headers included.** Accept: the posture ruled for a webhook's `headers` (`credential: 'map'`), and a map's entries cannot be told apart. Consequence to name on a card: `GET /packages/:id/export` reads the served view, so an exported package re-imported elsewhere loses `headers`, `defaultHeaders`, `transport.headers` and `transport.env`, exactly as it loses a webhook's `headers` today. Follow-up, not blocking.
- **(5) Rows with an inline value at an undeclared `auth` key keep it at rest via carry-forward.** Accept: the datasource posture (#8081 item 3), and the carry-forward never creates cleartext; `_diagnostics` is the inventory. Follow-up: the stored-row migration that moves such a value into the credential store, filed from the private report, not described publicly.
- **(6) URL-borne credentials in `providerConfig.baseUrl` / `transport.url` not redacted.** Follow-up, not a must-fix on this PR: the gap predates it and nothing here widens it, and the datasource redactor's URL scrub shows the shape (scrub on read, carry forward on save). File it from the private report at the severity the QA report gives it.
- **Boot door (from ① item 2).** Should-fix on the prose: one sentence in the changeset that the artifact load at boot and reload parses the same schema, and that an artifact `os build` wrote carries no undeclared key. Not blocking.

### ④ Design judgment

- `packages/spec/src/shared/connector-auth.zod.ts` — holds against ADR-0143 D3 / Acceptance and ADR-0097 §3, and against its first consumer: `ConnectorInstanceAuthSchema` is a `discriminatedUnion('type')`, so a body routes to one member and the member's terminal refusal is the one issue at `auth`; the `superRefine` on the entry does not add to it. The shared `history` sentence is true of the four kinds. Tried: a spelling outside `guidance` (`apiKey` on `bearer`) is still refused, with the distance fallback and no suggestion that lands on a tombstone; `none` with `credentialRef` is refused with a prescription naming a kind that takes one. No finding.
- `packages/spec/src/integration/connector-credential-redaction.ts` — holds against the registry contract (pure, returns the input by reference when nothing is withheld, sorted dotted `redactedKeys`, `_diagnostics` untouched) and against the carry-forward's path grammar (key hops only, no arrays). Reading the declared keys from the union through `wrapperChainOf` / `objectShapeOf` / `zodDefOf` covers a kind added later and both nested unions. Two should-fixes, both follow-ups: (a) a non-object `auth` or `authentication` is served as stored (① item 6); withholding a non-record at those two positions, as the map positions already do, closes it in a line. (b) `CONNECTOR_CREDENTIAL_MAP_PATHS` names four provider-owned positions by hand; a provider plugin that introduces another header or environment map under `providerConfig` is not covered, and the census guards only the `auth` kinds. A provider-declared credential-position contract is the durable form; a card, not this PR.
- `packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-type-redaction.ts` — one registration line and its note; holds. The built-in placement is the measured fail-open argument the module already makes for `datasource`, and `listMetadataTypeRedactorTypes` lists it. No finding.
- `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.connector-instance-auth-inline-secret-refused.ts` — holds: the id is the one the changeset marker names, the four fields follow the sibling entry, the prescription matches the shapes as declared (`api-key` with optional `headerName` / `paramName`, `basic` with `username`), and the acceptance names a route that exists (`GET /api/v1/automation/connectors`, the `ready` state the dogfood waits on). No finding.
- The three spec test files and the dogfood file were read, not reviewed: every value is a placeholder and every read assertion is an absence; the dogfood seeds the stored row through the system context and pins that the stored row itself is never redacted.

Must-fixes: none. Should-fixes (follow-up cards, none blocking): the non-record `auth` / `authentication` fail-closed line; the provider-declared credential positions contract; the export round trip losing provider maps; the URL-borne credential scrub; the boot-door sentence in the changeset.
